description: Hatchet workload, queue, and worker health from Hatchet's Prometheus endpoint and engine OTLP gauges.

options.content:
**Answers:** is work flowing, and do workers keep up?

- **Overview** holds the golden signals: traffic (tasks created), errors (task failure rate), latency (queue wait, run duration), and saturation (queued tasks, slot utilization).
- Rows go from workload to workers. The collapsed row holds container limits.
- **Sources:** Hatchet's Prometheus endpoint (`job="hatchet"`: tasks, queues, workers) and engine OTLP gauges (engines reporting, concurrency slots, SDKs).
- **Filters:** Service, Environment, Namespace, and Host apply to OTLP panels; Worker and Workflow to endpoint panels. Click a worker or workflow in its table to filter by it.

panels.title: Engines reporting
panels.description: Hatchet engine processes exporting OTLP metrics within Prometheus' 5-minute lookback. 0 means the engine is down or cannot reach otel-collector-agent.

panels.title: Live workers
panels.description: Workers the scheduler can assign tasks to. A worker that stops heartbeating drops out.

panels.title: Tasks created
panels.description: Tasks created in the selected range by triggers, events, schedules, and crons.

defaults.noValue: No data: needs SERVER_PROMETHEUS_ENABLED on Hatchet

panels.title: Task failure rate
panels.description: Share of finished tasks (succeeded plus failed) in the selected range that failed. Retries are counted separately.

defaults.noValue: No data: needs SERVER_PROMETHEUS_ENABLED on Hatchet

panels.title: Queue wait p95
panels.description: 95th percentile time from queued to assigned to a worker, across all workflows, in the selected range. The largest bucket is 15 s.

defaults.noValue: No tasks assigned in this time range

panels.title: Queued tasks
panels.description: Tasks waiting for a worker slot now, across all queues.

panels.title: Busiest worker
panels.description: Highest slot utilization among live workers now. Near 100% while tasks queue means that worker is the bottleneck; the Workers table shows which one.

panels.title: Run duration p95
panels.description: 95th percentile run duration of completed workflows, across all workflows, in the selected range.

defaults.noValue: No completed runs in this time range

panels.title: Task throughput
panels.description: Tasks created and finished per second. Created staying above finished means the backlog grows.

defaults.noValue: No data: needs SERVER_PROMETHEUS_ENABLED on Hatchet

panels.title: Task latency
panels.description: 95th percentile queue wait (left axis) and completed-run duration (right axis) across all workflows. Run duration excludes queue time.

defaults.noValue: No tasks assigned or finished in this time range

panels.title: Task outcomes
panels.description: Finished, retried, and rescheduled tasks per second across tenants. Scheduling timed out means no worker slot freed up before the task's schedule timeout.

defaults.noValue: No data: needs SERVER_PROMETHEUS_ENABLED on Hatchet

panels.title: Run duration p95 by workflow
panels.description: 95th percentile execution time of completed runs (start to finish, excluding queue time) per workflow; a DAG counts as one run.

defaults.noValue: No runs finished in this time range

panels.title: Queued tasks by queue
panels.description: Tasks waiting for a worker slot, by queue (one queue per task action). Workers do not own queues: any live worker that registered the action can take the task. Polled every 15 s.

panels.title: Queue wait p95 by workflow
panels.description: 95th percentile time from queued to assigned to a worker, per workflow. The largest bucket is 15 s, so waits above 15 s show as 15 s.

defaults.noValue: No tasks assigned in this time range

panels.title: Workflow summary
panels.description: Per-workflow runs, failure shares, and completed-run duration over the selected range, plus queue wait and the current backlog.

panels.title: Workers
panels.description: Live workers as the scheduler sees them: running tasks (used slots), slot capacity, and utilization. Workers that stop heartbeating drop out. Hatchet exports no task durations per worker; use Workflow summary for p95 per workflow.

panels.title: Running tasks by worker
panels.description: Tasks occupying worker slots, by worker name. Workers sharing a name are summed; the Workers table splits them by ID.

panels.title: Slot utilization by worker
panels.description: Used slots as a share of each worker's slots. A worker pinned near 100% while its queues grow needs more slots or more replicas.

panels.title: Live workers
panels.description: Workers the scheduler can assign tasks to. A worker that stops heartbeating drops out.

panels.title: Running and queued tasks
panels.description: Tasks occupying worker slots next to tasks waiting for one. A queued line that keeps rising means workers cannot keep up.

panels.title: Concurrency-controlled tasks
panels.description: Tasks held by the scheduler's in-memory concurrency indexes. Running tasks occupy a concurrency slot; queued tasks wait for one. A growing queued line means concurrency limits are holding work back. Appears once a workflow uses a concurrency strategy.

panels.title: Active SDKs
panels.description: Live workers by SDK language, SDK version, runtime, and OS. Use it to track SDK upgrades across workers. OTEL gauges keep the last value of each label set until the engine restarts, so a tenant, table, or SDK that stops reporting holds its last value.

panels.title: CPU throttled periods
panels.description: Share of CFS scheduling periods in which the container hit its cpus limit. Sustained throttling slows scheduling and raises latency; raise the container's cpus limit.

panels.title: CPU throttled time
panels.description: Seconds per second that the container's threads spent throttled by its cpus limit.

panels.title: Memory limit hits
panels.description: Times the container's memory usage reached its mem_limit in each interval. Repeated hits precede OOM kills; raise the container's mem_limit.
